feature: Spotlight: dim and blur everything but one area
summary: The Lens tool has a seventh kind, Spotlight. Drag a box round anything and the box stays exactly as it was while everything else on the picture goes darker, softer, or both. It is a live layer: move it, resize it, round it, make it an ellipse, soften its edge, retune it any time.
setup: Photonz Dev, release Next, no flag changed from its default. Any screenshot. Walks: spotlight-lens-walk (picture) and spotlight-on-a-video-walk (a screen recording), both at Next defaults, both photographed the real window.

try.do: Open a screenshot, press K for the Lens tool, and in the panel's Lens Tool section set Does to Spotlight.
Drag a box round one button or row. Everything outside it goes darker and a little softer; the box is untouched.
In the Lens section, pull Blur to 0 for dim only.
Pull Dim to 0 and Blur up for blur only.
Pull Feather up to soften the edge round the box.
Set Shape to Ellipse, or set a Corner Radius in Appearance for a rounded box.
Drag the box somewhere else, or drag a handle to resize it; the lit area follows.
Open a screen recording and do the same: the spotlight lands as its own track over the clip.

evaluate: Is Lens > Does > Spotlight where you would look for this, or would you expect it as its own tool?
Are Dim 50% and Blur 4 pt the right starting point for highlighting a button?
Does the Feather edge look natural, or should it reach into the box as well as out?
Should the spotlight be able to wear a ring (Effects > Border) round the lit area?
rough: No mock covers a spotlight or the Lens panel, so there is no side-by-side; the rows follow the Lens and Magnify sections already in the panel.
Chose a Spotlight kind on the existing Lens tool over a new tool, because it is the same gesture (drag a box) and the same kind of layer (changes what is under it), and the tool bar stays as it is.

Chose Dim to scale the colour values, so Dim 50% is half as bright to the eye in either mixing setting. Measured on a striped picture: outside mean luma 127.5 to 63.5 (ratio 0.498) in light, 127.5 to 64.0 (0.502) in sRGB, inside unchanged at 127.5. A plain Lens cannot pass that bar: it only ever changes what is inside its box, so the outside ratio stays 1.0.
Chose a feather that lies wholly outside the box, so what you lit is pixel-identical at any feather (unit tested at feather 0 and 30).

Frame time, 12 megapixel picture with 10 layers, wall clock to a finished image on this Mac: no spotlight 4.5 ms; dragging Dim 6.7 ms median; dragging Blur 10.9 ms median; dragging Feather 7.1 ms median (19 ms before the feather blur was limited to the area's neighbourhood); a window-sized patch with dim and blur 6.0 ms median. First frame of a drag peaks at about 20 ms. The canvas on screen matched a fresh render on every frame of the walk's drags (0.00% differing).
A spotlight's own Border, Shadow and Blur effects do nothing yet: only Opacity, Blending and Corner Radius from Appearance apply to it.
On a video it works through the same drawing, but every frame now blurs the whole frame while a spotlight with Blur is on screen; not measured during playback.
An agent cannot set a spotlight's rows yet (nor any lens's kind or amount); a field for it did not fit in Ask's first request, which had 14 tokens to spare.
